research.question: Can the reported BTC timing comparison be independently reproduced?
research.target_claim: The paper reports wealth 14.41 and 6094.94, Sharpe 1.01 and 2.81 for ledgers A and F.

source_facts.assertion: BTCUSDT daily, 20-day close momentum, trailing 90-observation sample z-score threshold 0.5, A lagged and F current positions on open-to-open returns, additive turnover cost 0.001, annualization 365.25.

project_choices.decision: Compare independently computed metrics to rounded paper figures with absolute tolerance 0.005 for Sharpe and 0.5% relative for wealth; report exact differences without adjustment.
Use first 3335 open-to-open returns, with zero final return and no forced liquidation; include warmup zeros in Sharpe.

uncertainties.statement: Authors' canonical replication code and original raw API responses unavailable; endpoint and source revisions may affect exact parity.

inputs: Paper PDF and four raw Binance daily BTCUSDT API pages
method.eligibility: Exactly 3336 continuous daily bars with positive finite prices and correct start and end timestamps.
method.transformations: Compute 20-day close momentum and 90-value sample z-score; flat during warmup. A uses prior signal on current open-to-open return, F uses current signal. Subtract 0.001 per absolute position change at corresponding bar; compound 1+net return. Sharpe is mean divided by sample standard deviation times sqrt(365.25). Explicitly distinguish close availability from bar-open credit timestamp.
method.comparison_rule: Report relative wealth and absolute Sharpe errors against table 1; parity requires both metrics for each ledger within the stated fixed tolerances. Failure to match is a complete unfavorable result.
method.inference_criterion: Descriptive deterministic reproduction; no statistical inference or claim about prevalence.

non_goals: ETH, equities, grid and gate calibration

study_owned.description: Decode, validate, evaluate and independently verify the timestamp and numerical computations.
